title: Google's price hike explanation ignores the real culprit: mandatory AI bloat
excerpt: Google is forcing you to pay more for Gemini
content_html:
Published Jul 29, 2026, 8:15 AM EDT

Jon Gilbert is a Features Writer for Android Police. I've covered Android since 2021, focusing on writing features and guides about Android apps and features that directly affect users. I've attended CES to uncover powerful hardware that isn't dominated by Google like the Mudita Kompakt. I trawl through Android news daily, hunting for stories that have real-world consequences. I hold a BA in History & Classics. 

To no one's surprise, Google will be raising prices on the Google Pixel 11 series of devices relative to the Pixel 10 series. Additionally, Google is reportedly increasing prices on current Pixel devices.

Google delivered this news in a statement last week, and on the surface, it merely confirms what we already knew. Hardware prices are rising, and manufacturers are passing the costs on to users.

However, when Google is exacerbating price increases, I find the statement insulting.

Google explains what we already knew

RAM is more expensive. Prices are rising. Who knew?

According to a statement given by Google's Vice President of Devices and Services, Shakil Barkat (via 9To5Google), the entire Pixel family of devices will see "price adjustments."

Statement: The brand will make these changes "dynamically to match supply realities."

Translation: Google will continue to raise prices to match hardware costs.

Statement: Google has “shielded our consumers from supply fluctuations for as long as possible.”

Translation: The Pixel 10 was the first Pixel since the Pixel 7 not to see a price rise.

Statement: Price changes will impact "in-market Pixel phones."

Translation: Expect price increases for the Pixel 10 series.

It's a lot of bad (if expected) news, but one statement stood out to me.

Barkat stated that the company is making a "dedicated effort" to reduce memory requirements on Android to "enable devices to have less RAM while maintaining a great user experience."

But how can Google drive down RAM requirements while promoting the most memory-hungry apps since Chrome?

Google's statement is at odds with its mobile strategy

It cannot lower prices while developing Gemini Intelligence

At Google I/O 2026, the company debuted Gemini Intelligence, the biggest change to Gemini since its launch. It has ominous consequences for the future of Android.

The subheading of Google's blog post covering the launch reads:

As Android transitions from an operating system into an intelligence system, your devices are becoming even more helpful with upgrades that will save you time.

The intention is clear. Gemini Intelligence is the future of Android. It works proactively, automating tasks in the background while you use your phone normally.

It sounds potentially useful, but there's an obvious problem.

Gemini Intelligence reserves a permanent chunk of RAM for AI tasks. That's why it's unavailable on any device with 8GB or less.

Remember how the Pixel 9a lacked features like Call Notes and Pixel Screenshots? It's because it only shipped with 8GB of RAM, so it had to use Gemini Nano 1.0 XXS, which couldn't handle these features.

So, 12GB is now the minimum requirement for a Pixel phone. That's part of the reason why Google is not reducing the Pixel 11's RAM to keep prices stable.

But 12GB is only the minimum requirement because of Google's decisions. This isn't only a case of Google pushing supply costs to the consumer; it is a case of Google exacerbating the problem.

8GB is enough RAM for a modern Android phone, but not for Google

An end to affordable Pixel A phones?

I've tolerated most Gemini-powered features as they're mostly optional. The only reason I regularly interact with the feature in my personal life is that Google replaced Assistant with Gemini on my smart speakers.

But if Google's implication that Gemini Intelligence will be a fundamental part of Android becomes reality, we could see an end to affordable 8GB devices like the Pixel 10a.

The Pixel 10a is a fantastic device. We rated it the best phone you can buy new for $500, and named it the perfect device for those new to Android or casual users. But that's not good enough for Google.

If Google makes Gemini Intelligence the new reality, it'll never be seen again on new Android phones.

Google is driving up the price we pay with its insistence on Gemini

Mandatory features that drive up prices

So 12GB of RAM is the new minimum memory requirement for Android phones. Why? So new Android phones can run Gemini Intelligence.

Google can shrug its shoulders and talk about "supplier costs" all it wants, but it's not making consumer-friendly decisions.

The Pixel 11 could be the same price as the Pixel 10 with no noticeable drop in performance. But in its blind desire to win the AI arms race, Google is saddling consumers with a bill for features they didn't ask for.

Imagine ordering a burger in a restaurant, then the chef brings out a wagyu steak on the side. What? Didn't you want that? Tough, you're paying for it anyway.

Google has made a token effort to compromise by pushing the minimum storage on the Pixel 11 to 256GB. But again, it was Google that installed apps that could use over 10GB of storage without informing you.

The Pixel 11 is a slap in the face for Pixel fans

Pixel phones have historically been good devices. I still recommend the Pixel 10 as the standout phone to buy.

I can understand the utility of Pixel Glow, and the new Google ecosystem looks neat.

But this statement has proved that Google is not interested in making any consumer-friendly decisions. All it cares about is the AI arms race, for which we're footing the bill.

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 7 月 29 日上午 8:15（美国东部时间）

乔恩·吉尔伯特 (Jon Gilbert) 是《Android Police》的专题作家。 我自 2021 年以来一直在报道 Android，专注于编写有关直接影响用户的 Android 应用和功能的功能和指南。 我参加 CES 是为了发现 Mudita Kompakt 等不由 Google 主导的强大硬件。 我每天都会浏览 Android 新闻，寻找对现实世界产生影响的故事。 我拥有历史与古典文学学士学位。

毫不奇怪，谷歌将相对于 Pixel 10 系列提高 Google Pixel 11 系列设备的价格。 此外，据报道，谷歌正在提高当前 Pixel 设备的价格。

谷歌上周在一份声明中公布了这一消息，表面上看，它只是证实了我们已经知道的事情。 硬件价格不断上涨，制造商正在将成本转嫁给用户。

然而，当谷歌加剧价格上涨时，我发现这种说法具有侮辱性。

谷歌解释了我们已经知道的事情

内存更贵。 价格正在上涨。 谁知道？

根据谷歌设备和服务副总裁 Shakil Barkat（来自 9To5Google）的声明，整个 Pixel 系列设备都将进行“价格调整”。

声明：该品牌将“动态地适应供应现实”进行这些改变。

翻译：谷歌将继续提高价格以匹配硬件成本。

声明：谷歌“尽可能长时间地保护我们的消费者免受供应波动的影响”。

翻译：Pixel 10 是自 Pixel 7 以来第一款价格没有上涨的 Pixel。

声明：价格变化将影响“市售 Pixel 手机”。

翻译：预计 Pixel 10 系列的价格会上涨。

这是很多坏消息（如果是预料之中的话），但有一个声明对我来说很突出。

Barkat 表示，该公司正在“致力于”减少 Android 的内存需求，以“使设备拥有更少的 RAM，同时保持良好的用户体验”。

但谷歌如何才能降低 RAM 需求，同时推广自 Chrome 以来最耗内存的应用程序呢？

谷歌的声明与其移动战略不一致

发展Gemini Intelligence的同时无法降低价格

在 Google I/O 2026 上，该公司首次推出了 Gemini Intelligence，这是 Gemini 自推出以来最大的改变。 它对 Android 的未来产生了不祥的后果。

谷歌关于此次发布的博客文章的副标题如下：

随着 Android 从操作系统转变为智能系统，您的设备在升级方面变得更加有帮助，从而节省您的时间。

意图很明确。 Gemini Intelligence 是 Android 的未来。 它会主动工作，在您正常使用手机时在后台自动执行任务。

这听起来很有用，但有一个明显的问题。

Gemini Intelligence 为 AI 任务保留了一块永久的 RAM。 这就是为什么它在任何 8GB 或以下的设备上不可用。

还记得 Pixel 9a 缺乏通话记录和 Pixel 屏幕截图等功能吗？ 因为它只配备了 8GB RAM，所以它必须使用 Gemini Nano 1.0 XXS，而它无法处理这些功能。

因此，12GB 现在是 Pixel 手机的最低要求。 这就是 Google 没有降低 Pixel 11 的 RAM 以保持价格稳定的部分原因。

但由于 Google 的决定，12GB 只是最低要求。 这不仅仅是谷歌将供应成本推给消费者的一个例子；这是谷歌加剧问题的一个例子。

8GB RAM 对于现代 Android 手机来说足够了，但对于 Google 来说就不够了

经济实惠的 Pixel A 手机即将终结吗？

我已经容忍了大多数 Gemini 驱动的功能，因为它们大多是可选的。 我在个人生活中经常使用该功能的唯一原因是 Google 在我的智能音箱上用 Gemini 取代了 Assistant。

但如果谷歌关于 Gemini Intelligence 将成为 Android 基本组成部分的暗示成为现实，我们可能会看到 Pixel 10a 等经济实惠的 8GB 设备的终结。

Pixel 10a 是一款出色的设备。 我们将其评为 500 美元能买到的最好的新手机，并称其为 Android 新手或普通用户的完美设备。 但这对谷歌来说还不够好。

如果谷歌让 Gemini Intelligence 成为新的现实，那么它将永远不会再出现在新的 Android 手机上。

谷歌对 Gemini 的坚持抬高了我们付出的代价

推高价格的强制性功能

因此，12GB RAM 是 Android 手机新的最低内存要求。 为什么？ 因此新的 Android 手机可以运行 Gemini Intelligence。

谷歌可以耸耸肩，随心所欲地谈论“供应商成本”，但它并没有做出对消费者友好的决定。

Pixel 11 的价格可能与 Pixel 10 相同，而且性能没有明显下降。 但谷歌盲目渴望赢得人工智能军备竞赛，却让消费者为他们不想要的功能支付账单。

想象一下在餐厅点一个汉堡，然后厨师在旁边端上一块和牛牛排。 什么？ 你不想这样吗？ 太难了，无论如何你都要付出代价。

谷歌象征性地做出了妥协，将 Pixel 11 的最小存储空间提高到了 256GB。 但同样，是 Google 在没有通知您的情况下安装了可以使用超过 10GB 存储空间的应用程序。

Pixel 11 对 Pixel 粉丝来说是一记响亮的耳光

Pixel 手机历来都是不错的设备。 我仍然推荐 Pixel 10 作为最值得购买的出色手机。

我能理解 Pixel Glow 的实用性，而且新的 Google 生态系统看起来很整洁。

但这一声明已经证明，谷歌无意做出任何有利于消费者的决定。 它关心的只是人工智能军备竞赛，而我们为此买单。
